adaptation: Standard layout adapted: the chart anchors on total money in (software revenue $125.4M + Bitcoin fair-value gain $20,912.4M = $21,037.8M) because Strategy's official income statement places the gain inside operating income. Flow balance checks on the adapted model: total money in = left after direct costs + cost of revenue ($21,037.8M = $21,002.0M + $35.8M); left after direct costs = operating income + operating expenses ($21,002.0M = $20,909.8M + $92.2M); operating income + other income − tax = net income ($20,909.8M + $32.5M − $1,409.3M = $19,533.0M). Reported figures are unchanged: revenue $125.4M, gross profit $89.6M (software only), operating income $20,909.8M, net income $19,533.0M.

kpis.label: Bitcoin gain
kpis.note: paper gain — no Bitcoin sold, no cash in

oneTimers: The $20.9B Bitcoin gain is not a one-off sale — it is a mark-to-market revaluation under accounting rule ASU 2023-08 (in force since January 1, 2025), which runs Bitcoin's price changes through earnings every quarter. It will be back next quarter, as a gain or a loss: over the first nine months of 2026 this same line nets to a $1.9B loss, because Q3's gain only partly undid earlier drops.

Between net income and what common shareholders 'got': $419.6M of dividends on Strategy's preferred stock, partly offset by a $5.5M deemed contribution from preferred repurchases — leaving $19,118.9M attributable to common stockholders.
otherDetail: Interest income of $47.1M on cash and short-term investments, minus $15.4M of interest expense on debt, plus $0.8M of other items — net +$32.5M.

segments.name: Bitcoin fair-value gain
segments.note: Strategy holds Bitcoin and marks it to market price every quarter (accounting rule ASU 2023-08). Bitcoin's price rose in Q3, so the stash was written up by $20.9B. No Bitcoin was sold and no cash arrived — this is a paper gain that reverses if the price falls.

segments.name: Software revenue
segments.note: The original business: analytics software — subscriptions ($68.6M), product support ($37.7M), licenses ($3.8M) and other services ($15.3M). Down 3% YoY as customers keep shifting from licenses to subscriptions.

sources.label: Official earnings release — Q3 2026 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Bitcoin's rising price added $20.9B to the value of Strategy's stash this quarter. No Bitcoin was sold and no cash changed hands. The same line was a net $1.9B loss over the first nine months of 2026 — it swings violently with Bitcoin's price, in both directions.
takeaways.title: A paper gain, not sales

takeaways.text: Software brought in $125.4M (-3% YoY) and earned $89.6M after direct costs — against $92.2M of running costs. Before the Bitcoin gain, operations lost $2.6M. The business is 0.6% of the money in this chart.
takeaways.title: The software business roughly broke even

takeaways.text: Strategy held 848,517 Bitcoin as of October 25, 2026 (847,666 at quarter-end, carried on the books at $70.8B) — accumulated largely with borrowed money and new stock issuance. The company is now, in effect, a Bitcoin holding company with a small software business attached.
takeaways.title: The bet keeps growing

verdict: Strategy reported $19.5B of profit, but almost none of it came from selling software — it is a $20.9B paper gain on the Bitcoin it holds, while the actual software business took in $125M and roughly broke even.
